problem: Consider the portion of the surface $z=x{y}^{2}$ whose projection onto the $xy$-plane is bounded by $y={x}^{2},$ $x=1,$ and the $x$-axis. Find a repeated integral expression for the surface area of this surface.
worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=f(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
z=x{y}^{2},\,(x,y)\in D
$$

where the region $D$ is given by

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14066535/assets/1419b067fe92945249655c5d29498aa4d3b0269d79ebd237fd9ed2a713b70b6a.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{2})={y}^{2}, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{2})=2xy,\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{({y}^{2})}^{2}+(2xy)^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{y}^{4}+4{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}\sqrt{1+{y}^{4}+4{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
